Thought: I need to identify the functional group that characterizes epoxides. Let me recall what an epoxide is in chemistry.

Epoxides are cyclic ethers that contain a three-membered ring consisting of an oxygen atom connected to two carbon atoms that are also bonded to each other. This three-membered ring structure is also called an oxirane ring.

Looking at the options:
A. A 3-membered oxirane ring - This is correct. Epoxides are characterized by a 3-membered ring containing an oxygen atom (oxirane ring).
B. A carboxylic acid - This is incorrect. Carboxylic acids contain a -COOH group, not characteristic of epoxides.
C. A double bonded oxygen - This is incorrect. While some oxygen-containing compounds have double-bonded oxygen (like ketones or aldehydes), epoxides specifically have a 3-membered ring with oxygen.
D. A hydroxyl group - This is incorrect. Hydroxyl groups (-OH) are characteristic of alcohols, not epoxides.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
